1.note: The name is transliterated as printed; the identification of this Ferrara merchant is uncertain.

2.he: דתלו בה טפלי שבה אל כמ"ר יום טוב
2.note: The phrasing is obscure. It may mean the widow, with dependent children, went back to live with her son, or that the coin passed to him.

3.note: The author's reading of the abbreviation. On actual Jewish shekels, these letters are generally read as a date (ש"ב, 'year 2', etc.).

4.note: The list ends with an unnamed 'Rabbi', presumably Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi, though the text may be truncated.

5.note: The word האר is unclear. It may be a variant spelling or a corruption; the sense 'from the Samaritan language' has been followed.

6.note: The reference is kept as the author gives it (Ikkarim 3:16).

7.note: The reference is kept as given. In modern editions, the passage on the shekel is Antiquities 3.8.2 (3.194).
